narrative:
On November 20, 2026, the Karnataka High Court registered an overall hearing clearance rate of 45.1%, taking up 1,187 of the 2,632 scheduled cases across 69 judges. This performance holds virtually steady with the prior day's 45.0% rate (1,285 of 2,853 heard on November 19) and mirrors the 44.0% clearance observed on November 13, remaining well above the 23.3% rate recorded on November 18.

Judge-wise performance showed high-volume output in Hall 16, where Justice R. Nataraj heard 101 of 175 scheduled cases (57.7%). Bench efficiency was notably strong for Jayant Banerji and N.V. Bhavani in Hall 3, clearing 25 of 31 matters (80.6%), while Justice Ravi V. Hosmani heard 43 of 52 cases (82.7%). In contrast, heavy list sizes hindered conversion elsewhere, such as Hall 12 where Justice S.R. Krishna Kumar heard 6 of 119 scheduled cases (5.0%).

Stage-level analysis highlights solid movement in early-stage proceedings. Orders achieved a 52.0% hearing rate (431 of 829), comparable to yesterday's 52.9%. Admission hearings improved to 50.6% (401 of 792) from 43.8% on November 19, and Final Hearings rose to 32.4% (110 of 340) from 22.5%. Further Hearing matters saw lower progress, converting only 13.9% (31 of 223).

Across case types, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest burden with 982 scheduled cases, converting 38.6% (379 heard), down from 45.8% yesterday. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) held steady at 45.9% (214 of 466 heard), while Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) reached 47.9% (190 of 397). Regular Second Appeals (RSA) saw strong clearance at 52.7% (125 of 237), outperforming Regular First Appeals (RFA) at 34.0% (71 of 209).
